title: Add average, above_average, and format_summary to Rust report library
description: The rust_report_gen library has sum, max_item, and min_item. Extend src/lib.rs with three new public functions: average, above_average, and format_summary. New tests are injected alongside existing ones.

task_spec.prompt:
Extend src/lib.rs with three new public functions:

  pub fn average(items: &[Item]) -> f64
    — return the mean value of all items; return 0.0 for empty slice

  pub fn above_average(items: &[Item]) -> Vec<&Item>
    — return items whose value is strictly above the average; empty slice -> empty vec

  pub fn format_summary(items: &[Item]) -> String
    — return a one-line summary string containing:
        "count: N", "sum: S", "avg: A", "max: <name>", "min: <name>"
      (exact float precision doesn't matter; round to nearest integer in the string)
      For empty slice, return "count: 0, sum: 0, avg: 0, max: -, min: -"

Existing 4 tests must still pass. New tests in tests/extended.rs must also pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: average returns 0.0 for empty slice, mean for non-empty
above_average returns items with value > average
All new tests in tests/extended.rs pass
followup_prompts: Good. Now add input validation and error handling to the feature you just implemented. What should happen with invalid, missing, or malformed inputs? Update the implementation and tests to cover those cases.
Run `cargo test` to verify everything including your new error handling. Fix any failures and confirm the feature is complete.
